channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) hopes to participate in 11-on-11 drills next week before playing in the preseason next month.
item.description: Fowler notes that Mahomes was mostly limited to 7-on-7 work during spring practices, as he recovers from two ligament tears in his left knee. The Chiefs will be “cautious” with Mahomes’ reps, and he has not yet been cleared to participate in 11-on-11 drills. Mahomes always prefers to take live reps in preseason play. If he can do so, one assumes he would be a near-lock to play in Week 1 against the Broncos, and Fowler says that the Chiefs “have been leaning into this Week 1 possibility.” Check back in the coming days to find out if Mahomes is indeed cleared for team drills next week. Chiefs veterans report for training camp on July 28th.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cowboys hired Will Grier as an offensive assistant.
item.description: Grier retired on July 15th, after a brief offseason stint on the Panthers’ roster. According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, Grier considered joining the Cowboys’ coaching staff earlier this offseason. He spent times on the Cowboys’ roster from 2021-22 and 2024-25. The 31-year-old former quarterback joins with a sharp offensive coaching staff to begin his new career.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Giants have been “highly impressed” by WR Malachi Fields.
item.description: Fowler goes so far as to say there are “shades” of former Giants WR Plaxico Burress “as far as style.” This is, perhaps, technically a true statement, but almost assuredly hyperbolic. Fields, a third-round rookie, landed on a depth chart chock-full of speedy role players. He brings a unique skill set with his 6'4/218 frame and jump-ball abilities. Carving out a role this season is possible, but not a given.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Front Office Sports’ Eric Fisher reports that the NFL has scheduled Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta for Feb. 13, 2028, confirming the 17-game schedule remains in place for 2027.
item.description: Earlier this week, Front Office Sports’ Mark Maske reported that NFL owners expect to finalize a contract extension with Roger Goodell “in the coming months.” The current CBA runs through March 2031, but the NFL is negotiating new broadcast deals and is apparently hoping to install an 18-game schedule during the current CBA. Keeping the commissioner in place makes sense in that regard.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Steelers signed No. 76 overall pick Drew Allar to a four-year contract.
item.description: This deal comes just as the Steelers are gearing up to begin training camp. Allar was selected with the No. 76 pick in this year’s draft and, if all goes to plan for the Steelers in their first year under Mike McCarthy, is expected to redshirt his rookie season. The Penn State product who threw for 7,402-61-13 in his career will spend plenty of time developing behind the scenes with his sights set on possibly earning the QB1 job for the Steelers next season. Allar has reportedly already undergone some serious overhauling, as it was reported in May that the team was “uninstalling everything” he learned about the position at Penn State. It sounds like Allar has a ways to go before being NFL ready, but it will be interesting to hear how he progresses throughout training camp and he’ll be a player to watch when the preseason starts up.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel said Christian Gonzalez has reported to training camp.
item.description: Vrabel was noncommittal about whether Gonzalez would participate in practice, instead saying he “would expect him to participate.” The fourth-year corner is in the midst of contract negotiations and could reset the cornerback market when he eventually agrees to an extension. Gonzalez reported to mandatory minicamp earlier this offseason but did not participate in full team drills, and there’s been some speculation he could opt to hold in at camp while waiting for a new deal. The Patriots will take the practice field for the first time on Saturday, whether or not Gonzalez joins them in full capacity will be something to watch for.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports free agent WR DeAndre Hopkins is “considering the possibility of a coaching career,” and is visiting with the Patriots on Friday.
item.description: Hopkins said last month that he would “love to play for a competitor” at this point in his career, so this comes as a bit of a surprise. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told Reiss that Hopkins is considering a coaching career, but it was not specified whether he is looking to join the Patriots’ staff this season or is simply kicking the tires on a future career change. Hopkins, 34, caught 22 passes for 330 yards and two touchdowns in a limited role with the Ravens last season and wouldn’t be much more than a role player on any team he would join for this season.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Speaking on the Breaking Big Blue podcast, ESPN’s Jordan Raanan said he believes Odell Beckham Jr. is the “leader in the clubhouse” to win the final WR spot in camp.
item.description: Things are just getting underway for the Giants as they open camp, so there’s a lot that could play out between now and then. Beckham, 33, signed with the Giants this offseason after pleading for one more chance with the team that originally drafted him in 2014, and got his wishes when he inked a one-year deal in June. Beckham did not suit up for a team last season and caught just nine passes for 55 scoreless yards in the nine games he appeared in for the Dolphins in 2024. We never expected him to make much of a fantasy impact even if he were higher on the depth chart, but Beckham securing the final spot in the WR room would all but cement his status as a lightly-used role player for the Giants this season.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Panthers placed EDGE Nic Scourton on injured reserve.
item.description: This was expected after it was reported on Thursday that Scourton suffered a torn ACL in the team’s first practice. Scourton reportedly sought a second opinion on his injury, but the decision to place him on injured reserve on Friday officially signals the end of his season. The second-year pass-rusher was expected to make a nice leap this season after popping up for five sacks as a rookie, but will now spend this season rehabbing in preparation for 2027.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said the team has had “productive” negotiations with Jacoby Brissett as they work toward a new contract.
item.description: Brissett reported to training camp and was practicing with the team on Thursday. Brissett is entering this season as the Cardinals’ QB1 but is currently set to play out the season on the final year of a two-year, $12.5 million contract he signed last season when he was backing up Kyler Murray. Brissett is reportedly seeking a pay raise for this season rather than an extension, and it sounds like a deal will eventually be reached by the two sides before the start of the season. Brissett was fourth in Thursday’s practice rotation, but that will change as he continues to get up to speed with the team after missing OTAs and minicamp.-Zachary Krueger
